title: Resumable streaming + schema validation for embeddings client (Python/TS)
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Problem: The current embeddings client has brittle pagination and streaming semantics across Python and TypeScript SDKs. Long queries or interrupted connections can lead to duplicate embeddings, inconsistent typed responses, and unclear error propagation to callers. This ticket implements a unified approach: resumable streaming cursors, explicit typed schema validation for responses, improved error taxonomy (retryable vs terminal with clear codes), and backpressure-friendly client-side buffering. Goals: reduce end-to-end latency variance, eliminate duplicate outputs on reconnect, and provide ergonomically typed responses for TS/Python users. This work touches client runtime codepaths, the embeddings pagination API contract, and documentation/examples for migration.
acceptance_criteria: Python and TypeScript SDKs expose a stable 'ResumableCursor' abstraction enabling pause/resume across network interruptions
Responses are validated against a documented JSON schema; SDKs raise descriptive errors when server payloads deviate
Pagination streaming supports checkpoint tokens that are opaque to callers and safe to persist/replay
Client implements idempotency checks to avoid duplicate embeddings when resuming
Benchmark: median embedding request latency for batched streaming remains within 1.15x of current baseline for 95th percentile sequence lengths
Comprehensive unit/integration tests and end-to-end demo in docs reproducing resume scenario
TypeScript clients return strongly-typed responses (embedding vector type + metadata) and Python client provides typed dataclasses / pydantic models
Error taxonomy documented with recommended retry policies; SDKs implement default retryable vs terminal classification
